Code evidence contradicts the claim: in src/mcp/schemas.ts line 184, summarize_target (FR-MCP-008) is backed by summarizeTarget — a lighter TARGET STATUS summary (status/type counts, blocked, implemented-not-verified, missing-evidence; FR-MCP-008 AC-2), NOT the release-readiness gate. By that same pattern, FR-MCP-035 fills a real gap — the not-yet-existing MCP exposure of the FR-FLOW-007/008 readiness contract. An MCP-only agent currently cannot invoke release readiness at all; summarize_target is not functionally substitutable (different function, different/lighter payload). all.capability: CLI sync-counts recomputes the index Status Summary and Requirement Type Summary cells from records, defaulting to a drift check, writing with --apply, and gating CI non-zero with --check.
all.reason: Partial overlap only, not true functional replacement. The recompute/reconcile core genuinely overlaps: v2.3.0 FR-NODE-018 (sync-index / syncIndexRollups, src/core/mutation/sync-index.ts:128-132) already recomputes the 00.index Status Summary + Requirement Type Summary from workspace.records with NO target filter (same GLOBAL arithmetic as v3 sync-counts, src/core/mutation/sync-counts.ts:103-104), writes those cells back, and supports a --dry-run preview plus a stale-snapshot guard. So the 1차 근거 is right that both belong to the same rollup-reconciliation family. BUT IR-CLI-044 (core FR-NODE-050) adds a capability the shipped sync-index does NOT provide: the --check CI-gate that returns a non-zero exit code when drift exists (CLI mutations.ts:680-681: exitCode 1 when cells.length > 0). sync-index has no --check option and only exits non-zero (5) on !result.ok — sync-index --dry-run reports drift but exits 0, so it cannot gate CI on drift. IR-CLI-044's defining statement ('gating CI non-zero with --check') is therefore unsatisfiable via FR-NODE-018 alone. It also inverts the default safety (sync-counts defaults to a read-only check; sync-index defaults to a mutating write) and was built as a separate coexisting core rather than a rename. Because the CI-gate/check capability is a genuine, non-subsumed functional delta, this is partial overlap, not feature substitution; per the conservative rule it resolves to NEW to avoid wrongful discard.

all.reason: True functional overlap confirmed by code, not just title similarity. The v3 REL-PARSE-002 ("Diagnostic dedup single-source read envelope fix") targets the double-inclusion where readDiagnostics (src/cli/commands/read.ts:80) concatenates workspace.diagnostics again on top of validateWorkspace output (whose first rule already spreads [...workspace.diagnostics] at src/core/validator/rules.ts:263). But the shipped, verified v2.3.0 REL-PARSE-002 ("Deduplicated and line-anchored diagnostics") already provides the exact observable capability: dedupeDiagnostics (src/core/diagnostic.ts:26-42, literally tagged // @req REL-PARSE-002) collapses the identical duplicate objects, and every read seam funnels through splitDiagnostics/summarizeDiagnostics (buildReadEnvelope summary.ts:34-35; validate command read.ts:450-451), so structural codes (SRS-E013/E014) already report byCode=1. Mapping the ACs: v3 AC-1/2/3 (no double count of structural/parser diagnostics) are subsumed by v2.3.0 AC-1 (deterministic dedupe key) and AC-4 which explicitly enumerates "malformed table diagnostics are not double counted when parser diagnostics and validator diagnostics are combined" — the identical parser-plus-validator seam; v3 AC-4 (red no-double-count test) is subsumed by v2.3.0 AC-4; v3 AC-5 (CLI/MCP/resource parity) is subsumed by v2.3.0 AC-3 plus its cli-mcp-parity.test.ts. Both requirements claim implementation in the exact same three files (diagnostic.ts, validator/rules.ts, cli/commands/read.ts) and share the same ID. The only v3-unique element is a source cleanup (removing the redundant concat instead of relying on dedup to mask it), an implementation refinement of an already-shipped capability, not a new capability — discarding it leaves no functional gap since dedup already yields correct counts at every output path. This meets the functional-replacement bar (not partial similarity): v2.3.0 fully substitutes for v3. The remap-table entry assigning REL-PARSE-004 is mechanical ID-collision renumbering, not a capability adjudication, and does not change the merits.
